q: How do I calculate the carbon footprint of handmade paper?
title: Handmade paper carbon footprint per kg
short: Add the cotton rag, waste paper or plant fibre used per kg of finished sheets, the pulping and drying energy, and any dyes and sizing. Divide the unit's energy by kg of good sheets made.

ul: Cotton rags, waste paper or plant fibre.
Air or heated drying and calendering.

p: Report per kg of finished sheets. Air drying uses far less energy than heated drying, so say which the unit uses.

example.title: Worked example: plant energy per kg (one month)
lines: Plant total: 3,436 / 8,000 = 0.429 kg CO2 per kg
Add fibre, dyes and sizing for the full figure
example.note: Inputs are illustrative; use your own bills and production records.

senseible: Senseible reads the plant's electricity bills (CEA grid factor 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh for FY 2024-25, CO2 Baseline Database version 21.0) and fuel invoices (IPCC 2006 defaults) into a fingerprinted Scope 1 and 2 record, the plant-level input to a per-unit figure. Bought-in materials go to the supplier evidence trail; product reports are self-declared drafts.
